sections.title: What does it mean?
sections.content: Hungarian verbs can show when an action happened. In this lesson you will learn to recognise the difference between a simple present form and a basic past form.

sections.title: How does it work?
sections.content: A common past-tense marker is -t. Compare tanulok, “I study”, with tanultam, “I studied”. Compare dolgozik, “he/she works”, with dolgozott, “he/she worked”.

sections.title: Why does it look like this?
sections.content: The past is not a separate word such as English did. Information about the past is built into the verb form. At A1 we first learn to recognise this pattern. Full past-tense production comes later.
Do not try to memorise the whole past tense yet. First train your eye to notice the past marker and connect it with words such as tegnap.
